astley-bridge.coverP1: The BL1 6 and BL1 7 postcodes — the streets off Blackburn Road and Belmont Road, Seymour Road, Thorns Road, the Crompton Way end, and on up through Sharples towards Eagley and Dunscar.
astley-bridge.coverP2: There is one flat call-out charge across the whole 20-mile area, so being at the north end of town costs you nothing extra. The only thing distance changes is how quickly I can be there, not the bill.
astley-bridge.calledH2: What I actually get called to in Astley Bridge
astley-bridge.calledP1: Astley Bridge is not one kind of house, and that is the thing worth knowing before anyone quotes you. It grew up in the second half of the 1800s as Lower Sharples, around the bridge over Astley Brook, so the older core is stone terraces on and behind the main road. Then it kept going — interwar and post-war semis, and the larger houses that climb north towards Sharples and Belmont Road.
astley-bridge.calledP2: That mix matters because the right answer in a stone terrace on Blackburn Road is often the wrong answer half a mile up the hill. One has solid walls, a tight flue route and a combi; the other has a cylinder, an airing cupboard and room to think about a heat pump.
astley-bridge.threeH2: Three things Astley Bridge calls me out for
astley-bridge.threeP: The ground rises as you go north out of town, the houses get bigger, and the systems change with them. Three jobs come round again and again.

threeCards.h: Solid stone walls, and what that does to a quote
threeCards.p: The Victorian terraces here are stone, built before cavity walls, so there is nothing to fill and the heat loss is what it is. That is not a reason to do nothing — it is a reason to size the radiators and the boiler off the actual house rather than off a rule of thumb. If somebody quotes you a boiler without asking what the walls are, they are guessing.

threeCards.h: Cylinders, not combis, once you get up the hill
threeCards.p: The bigger houses towards Sharples and Belmont Road tend to have a hot water cylinder rather than a combi, and often an unvented one. Servicing an unvented cylinder needs a separate ticket beyond Gas Safe — the Unvented Hot Water Storage Systems certificate, under G3 of the Building Regulations. I hold it, and it is worth asking anyone who touches yours whether they do.

threeCards.h: Coming off an old system, without pretending it is like-for-like
threeCards.p: Plenty of the semis still have a regular system, or the scar of a back boiler, and swapping to a combi is a bigger job than a straight change. Pipework, flue route and where the boiler ends up all move. I would rather price that honestly after a look than give you a headline figure that changes on the day.

astley-bridge.costsP: Every figure below is the same in Astley Bridge as it is on my own street. Heat pumps and bathrooms are quoted after a survey rather than off a price list.

The certificate is completed on site and emailed before I leave, and the appliance is registered with the manufacturer on your behalf.
I remind you at about eleven months, so the next service does not creep up on you.

faqs.h: How quickly can you get to Astley Bridge?
faqs.p: About three miles, so it is inside the area where same-day is realistic when there is a slot. I will give you an honest date rather than promise a time I cannot keep.

faqs.h: My house is stone with no cavity. Is a heat pump a waste of time?
faqs.p: Not automatically, but it is a survey question rather than a phone question. It comes down to what the heat loss actually is, whether the radiators can run at a lower temperature, and where the cylinder would go. If the house is not ready, I will tell you that instead of selling you one.

Yes. It needs a separate ticket beyond Gas Safe and I hold it — the Unvented Hot Water Storage Systems certificate, in compliance with G3 of the Building Regulations. It is worth checking that whoever works on yours has it.

faqs.h: Do you work alongside builders on bigger projects?
faqs.p: Yes, regularly. Bathrooms and refurbishments get quoted in days with materials invoiced separately at cost, so you can see exactly what the work costs and exactly what the parts cost.

astley-bridge.closingP: If you are in Astley Bridge and want a straight answer on a boiler, a cylinder or a bathroom, the price is on the page and the diary is open.

great-lever.calledH2: What I actually get called to in Great Lever
great-lever.calledP1: Great Lever filled up fast. The population went from about 5,400 in 1891 to roughly 17,000 today, and most of the housing that went up in that first rush is still standing — dense two-up two-down terraces, built quickly, close together, with the yard and the back alley behind.
great-lever.calledP2: That shapes almost every job here. Rooms are small, so boiler and radiator sizing is not the same sum as it is in a semi. Flue routes are tight when your gable is a party wall and your back wall looks onto an alley. And a lot of these houses have had a bathroom added over the back kitchen at some point, which is its own set of problems.

great-lever.threeP: A street of terraces built to the same pattern tends to produce the same three jobs, over and over.

threeCards.h: Getting a combi in where a back boiler used to be
threeCards.p: Take the back boiler out and you are not doing a like-for-like swap — you are moving where the heat comes from, re-routing pipework, dealing with the old flue and finding somewhere sensible for the new boiler to live. It is a good job when it is done properly and a mess when it is rushed. I price it after a look, not off a list.

threeCards.h: The bathroom over the back kitchen
threeCards.p: Where a bathroom has been built onto the back of a terrace, the hot water has a long cold run to make before it arrives, and the pressure upstairs is often disappointing. That is usually pipework and layout rather than the boiler being too small — which matters, because replacing the boiler will not fix it.

threeCards.h: Landlord gas safety records, done on time
threeCards.p: A lot of these terraces are let, and a gas safety record is £99 for the first appliance and £10 for each one after it. Add a full boiler service at the same visit and it is £150 all in — that is the boiler on the certificate, with the £10 per extra appliance still applying. ainsworth.calledP1: Ainsworth is a stone village rather than a Bolton suburb, and it is worth saying plainly that it sits in Bury Council's area, not Bolton's, even though the postcode is BL2 and the road signs point at Bolton. That changes nothing about what I charge or how quickly I can get there. It does change who you talk to about anything that needs council consent.
ainsworth.calledP2: The building stock is genuinely different from the rest of my patch. Most of it is local buff-grey sandstone laid in courses, much of it from the early 1800s onwards, including the row of back-to-back cottages built for quarry workers around 1830 on Church Street and Delph Lane. There are six Grade II listed buildings in the village, and the old centre is a conservation area.
ainsworth.threeH2: Three things Ainsworth calls me out for
ainsworth.threeP: Solid stone walls, small old cottages and a protected village centre between them produce a fairly specific set of problems.

threeCards.h: Solid stone walls, and sizing the system for them honestly
threeCards.p: These houses were built long before cavity walls, so there is no cavity to fill and the heat loss is higher than a modern house of the same size. That is not a reason to oversize a boiler and hope — it is a reason to work the heat loss out properly and size the radiators to match. A boiler quoted without anyone asking about the walls is a boiler quoted on a guess.

threeCards.h: Anything that changes the outside of the building
threeCards.p: The old village is a conservation area with several listed buildings in it. A new flue terminal, external pipework or a heat pump unit outside can all need permission that would be nobody's business at all a mile down the road. I will tell you if I think your job is one of those, so you can check with Bury Council before anything is ordered rather than after it is fitted.

threeCards.h: Flue routes in a back-to-back cottage
threeCards.p: The quarry workers' cottages are genuinely back-to-back, which means there is no rear wall to terminate a flue on and the options are limited to the front, the roof, or moving the boiler. It is solvable, and it is the sort of thing worth establishing before you buy an appliance rather than on the morning of the fit.
